content.value_statement: Teams often struggle to keep Tailwind interfaces consistent across products. This skill provides reusable token, component, layout, theme, and accessibility patterns.
actual_capabilities: Defines semantic Tailwind color tokens with CSS variable themes.
Shows CVA variant patterns for buttons, cards, forms, grids, and dialogs.
Guides responsive container and grid design with Tailwind classes.
Provides dark mode provider and theme toggle examples.
Includes accessibility guidance for labels, error states, ARIA, and focus rings.
Documents class composition utilities with clsx and tailwind-merge.
limitations: Provides guidance and examples; it does not install packages automatically.
Assumes React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and common UI libraries.
Example components may need adaptation to local project conventions.
Does not run visual regression or accessibility tests by itself.

use_cases.title: Design System Foundation
use_cases.description: Plan semantic tokens, dark mode variables, and reusable Tailwind conventions for a new product interface.

use_cases.title: Component Library Standardization
use_cases.description: Convert repeated Tailwind markup into typed reusable components with consistent variants and states.

use_cases.title: Responsive UI Cleanup
use_cases.description: Improve layout consistency with container, grid, spacing, and accessibility patterns across existing screens.

prompt_templates.title: Map Design Tokens
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Tailwind design system skill to propose semantic color, spacing, radius, and dark mode tokens for my app.

prompt_templates.title: Create Component Variants
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Tailwind design system skill to design button, input, card, and label variants for a React TypeScript component library.

prompt_templates.title: Standardize Responsive Layouts
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Tailwind design system skill to define responsive container and grid patterns for dashboard, marketing, and form pages.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Existing UI System
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Tailwind design system skill to audit my current Tailwind components and create a migration plan for tokens, variants, themes, and accessibility.

output_examples.input: Plan a Tailwind token system for a SaaS dashboard.
output: Semantic color groups for background, foreground, primary, secondary, muted, accent, border, and ring states.
Dark mode variables that mirror the same token names.
Radius and spacing guidance for consistent component density.
A component inventory grouped by purpose, variant, size, and state.
Recommendations for shared variant naming and default states.
Accessibility checks for focus rings, disabled states, and readable contrast.

output_examples.input: Improve responsive layouts in an existing product.
output: Container sizes matched to common page types.
Grid rules for two, three, four, and six column layouts.
Review notes for spacing, wrapping, and mobile readability.

best_practices: Use semantic tokens before component-specific Tailwind classes.
Keep component variants typed, centralized, and documented.
Validate focus states, ARIA behavior, contrast, and dark mode together.
anti_patterns: Hardcoding brand colors inside every component.
Adding arbitrary values for common layout choices.
Copying example components without adapting project conventions.

faq.question: Does this skill create a full design system?
faq.answer: It provides patterns, examples, and implementation guidance. You still choose final tokens, components, and review standards.

faq.question: Can it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What frameworks does it assume?
faq.answer: The examples focus on React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, CVA, Radix patterns, and common utility helpers.

faq.question: Does it include accessibility guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers focus rings, ARIA error messages, labels, disabled states, and keyboard-friendly component structure.

faq.question: Can it help with dark mode?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes CSS variable theming, a theme provider pattern, and a theme toggle pattern.

faq.question: Will it modify my code automatically?
faq.answer: No. It is an instructional skill that guides implementation and review.
